section_summary: This section chiefly concerns Allied-occupation controls on entry into and departure from Japan, including diplomatic acknowledgments of SCAP Circular No. 8 and procedures for obtaining military clearance. It also documents baggage and automobile restrictions for returning Japanese nationals, applications by Catholic religious sisters seeking to teach in Japan, Spanish diplomatic travel, and several individual repatriation or commercial-travel cases. Internal memoranda show the State Department coordinating with the Joint Chiefs of Staff, Commerce Department, foreign embassies, and occupation authorities.

subfiles.title: Indexing note concerning the Alscap letter
subfiles.from: M. E. Wolberg, Special Projects Division
subfiles.about: Correct indexing of Alscap Inc.'s January 29 letter.
subfiles.summary: Directs that the Alscap letter be moved from a Visa Division number to the DC/R file.

subfiles.title: Alscap inquiry about sending Michel Scapa to Japan
subfiles.about: Visa requirements for a Greek employee's proposed business visit to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Alscap asks what visa requirements Michel Scapa must satisfy for planned travel from Europe to Japan and the Far East.

subfiles.title: Security checks on Michel Scapa and Alscap Inc.
subfiles.from: M. E. Wolberg, Special Projects Division
subfiles.about: Results of internal checks on Scapa and his employer.
subfiles.summary: VD, ES, and FC reported no information concerning Michel Scapa, while ES also found nothing on Alscap Inc.

subfiles.title: Reply denying private business travel to Japan
subfiles.from: Richard E. Hibbard, Special Projects Division
subfiles.about: Current military policy barring business and other private travelers from Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hibbard explains that occupation authorities presently prohibit business or private entry and advises watching for a public relaxation of restrictions.

subfiles.title: Subject card for control of entry and exit from Japan
subfiles.about: Foreign interests and Japanese entry-and-exit controls.
subfiles.summary: Subject card identifies the file as concerning control of individuals, aircraft, and surface vessels entering or leaving Japan.

subfiles.title: Uruguayan acknowledgment of Circular No. 8
subfiles.to: George C. Marshall, U.S. Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledgment and transmission to Uruguay of regulations governing travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The ambassador acknowledges the January 17 circular note and reports forwarding it to the Uruguayan government.

subfiles.title: Latvian acknowledgment of Circular No. 8
subfiles.about: Receipt of SCAP regulations controlling entry into and exit from Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Latvian Minister acknowledges receipt of the January 17 note and two copies of SCAP Circular No. 8.

subfiles.title: Nicaraguan acknowledgment of Circular No. 8
subfiles.about: Receipt and referral to Nicaragua of Japanese travel-control regulations.
subfiles.summary: The ambassador acknowledges Circular No. 8, forwards it to his government, and notes the Department's offer to transmit qualifying applications.

subfiles.title: Finnish acknowledgment of Circular No. 8
subfiles.about: Receipt and onward transmission of SCAP entry-and-exit regulations.
subfiles.summary: Finland's minister acknowledges the circular and reports sending the information to the appropriate Finnish authorities.

subfiles.title: Memorandum transmitting revised baggage letter for clearance
subfiles.from: Richard E. Hibbard, Special Projects Division
subfiles.to: D. O. Bowman, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Clearance of revised baggage rules for Japanese nationals returning home.
subfiles.summary: Hibbard submits a redrafted Commerce Department letter incorporating military rules for importing personally owned motor vehicles into Japan.

subfiles.title: Telephone conversation about amended export regulations
subfiles.from: M. E. Wolberg, Special Projects Division
subfiles.about: Publication and amendment of baggage export rules for returning Japanese nationals.
subfiles.summary: Kennedy advised that Comprehensive Export Schedule No. 23 was delayed and identified amendments deleting a food sentence and motor-vehicle provisions. She promised Wolberg copies when available.

subfiles.title: Telephone conversations on excluding motor vehicles from Japanese baggage
subfiles.from: M. E. Wolberg, Special Projects Division
subfiles.about: Commerce Department coordination over baggage rules and vehicle restrictions.
subfiles.summary: Thomas agreed that returning Japanese could be informed of general baggage rules while being barred from taking motor vehicles. Because customs enforcement would be difficult, travelers would risk confiscation in Japan, and Commerce would retain discretion over instructions to collectors.

subfiles.title: Development of baggage regulations for returning Japanese nationals
subfiles.from: M. E. Wolberg, Special Projects Division
subfiles.about: Selection of applicable Commerce Department export-license rules.
subfiles.summary: Wolberg and Thomas initially agreed to apply personal-baggage rules comparable to those used for Germans returning to Germany. After learning of later revisions from Weymueller and Kennedy, they decided the proposed letter should cite forthcoming Comprehensive Export Schedule No. 23.

subfiles.title: JK objection to permitting returning Japanese to import automobiles
subfiles.from: Mr. Martin, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.to: M. E. Wolberg, Special Projects Division
subfiles.about: Policy objections to including passenger vehicles among permissible personal effects.
subfiles.summary: JK argues that SCAP intended to allow essential household and professional effects, not vehicles, and that Japan's economy, roads, and fuel shortages make automobile imports undesirable.

subfiles.title: Handwritten acknowledgment note on travel regulations
subfiles.about: Acknowledgment of the January 17 note on regulations for private travelers.
subfiles.summary: Fragmentary note records acknowledgment of the January 17 communication concerning regulations applicable to private individuals.

subfiles.title: Ecuadorian acknowledgment of Japanese travel requirements
subfiles.about: Receipt of the January 17 note describing requirements for travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Ecuador's chargé acknowledges and takes note of the requirements applicable to persons wishing to travel to Japan.

subfiles.title: Egyptian acknowledgment of Circular No. 8
subfiles.about: Receipt of Circular No. 8 and its application procedures.
subfiles.summary: The Egyptian Ambassador acknowledges the January 17 note, two copies of Circular No. 8, and its procedures for submitting applications.

subfiles.title: Letter to Commerce on baggage and vehicle rules for returning Japanese
subfiles.from: Edward G. Hunt, Special Projects Division
subfiles.to: John C. Borton, Office of International Trade Operations
subfiles.about: Application of personal-baggage export rules and military automobile restrictions.
subfiles.summary: The Department proposes applying Comprehensive Export Schedule No. 23 to self-financed Japanese returnees. Household and professional effects are allowed; motor vehicles must have been bona fide personal property for at least one year and cannot be imported for sale.

subfiles.title: Handwritten acknowledgment note concerning military travel controls
subfiles.about: Receipt of a January 17 note concerning military travel rules.
subfiles.summary: Fragmentary annotation records acknowledgment of a verbal note about military controls associated with travel to Japan.

subfiles.title: Panamanian acknowledgment of Circular No. 8
subfiles.about: Modified military-permission requirements for civilian travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Panama acknowledges the January 17 note and Circular No. 8 and reports forwarding the documents to its government.

subfiles.title: Brazilian acknowledgment of Japanese entry-and-exit instructions
subfiles.about: Receipt and transmission of new Allied instructions concerning Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Brazilian Embassy acknowledges the January circular and reports retransmitting its instructions to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

subfiles.title: Irish request to add Joan Twomey to a party of sisters
subfiles.about: Permission for a sixth Irish sister to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Ireland adds Joan Twomey to five Drishane Convent sisters seeking entry and requests an early decision before their planned sailing from Cobh.

subfiles.title: Haitian acknowledgment of Circular No. 8
subfiles.about: Receipt of revised Allied controls on people, aircraft, and vessels entering or leaving Japan.
subfiles.summary: Haiti acknowledges the January circular and thanks the Department for offering assistance to Haitian nationals under the revised procedures.

subfiles.title: Telegram reporting clearance of Johan Brandt
subfiles.about: Military clearance for Johan Brandt to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Reports that Johan Brandt, traveling from Norway through the United States, was cleared to enter Japan as adviser to the Norwegian Mission.

subfiles.title: Salvadoran acknowledgment of Circular No. 8
subfiles.about: Receipt and transmission of SCAP's current entry-and-exit regulations.
subfiles.summary: The ambassador thanks the Secretary for Circular No. 8 and reports transmitting it to the government of El Salvador.

subfiles.title: Cuban acknowledgment of revised Japan travel procedures
subfiles.about: Receipt of the January 17 note and SCAP Circular No. 8.
subfiles.summary: Cuba acknowledges the modified procedure for civilian travel to and from Japan and forwards the note and circular to its government.

subfiles.title: Lebanese acknowledgment of Circular No. 8
subfiles.about: Receipt of current SCAP regulations for Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Lebanese Minister acknowledges receipt of the January 17 communication and copies of Circular No. 8.

subfiles.title: Dominican acknowledgment of Japanese entry-and-exit regulations
subfiles.about: Receipt of regulations controlling people, aircraft, and vessels traveling to or from Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Dominican chargé acknowledges and thanks the Secretary for the January note and accompanying circular.

subfiles.title: Victor S. Reuben postpones travel to Japan
subfiles.about: Return of Reuben's unused military permit after postponement.
subfiles.summary: Miss Eads reports that Reuben cannot travel until after March and will reapply, allowing his existing permit to be returned.

subfiles.title: Letter concerning repatriation from Okinawa to Argentina
subfiles.about: Financing the repatriation of Guillermo Yuen Nakamatsu and Maria del Valle Idiarte de Nakamatsu.
subfiles.summary: The Department relays that the Nakamatsus lack passage funds. Argentina could guarantee payment, but travel must be through the United States; estimated Okinawa–West Coast fares are supplied, and Argentina is asked for further instructions.

subfiles.title: Charge slip for repatriation enclosure
subfiles.about: Administrative tracking of an enclosure concerning the Nakamatsu repatriation case.
subfiles.summary: Charge slip records circulation and filing of the enclosure concerning travel from Okinawa to Argentina.

subfiles.title: Yokohama airgram on the Nakamatsu repatriation case
subfiles.from: Johnson, Yokohama Branch, Office of the U.S. Political Adviser
subfiles.about: Lack of passage funds for two Okinawa residents seeking repatriation to Argentina.
subfiles.summary: The Yokohama office reports that the Nakamatsus cannot pay passage. Argentina could guarantee the fare, and repatriation would have to proceed through a U.S. West Coast port.

subfiles.title: Honduran acknowledgment of modified Japan travel rules
subfiles.to: George C. Marshall, U.S. Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Receipt of the January 17 note modifying travel procedures for Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Honduran Ambassador acknowledges the note concerning travel into and from Japan and indicates that it was transmitted to Honduras.

subfiles.title: Irish note giving Joan Twomey's religious name
subfiles.about: Additional identification and destination information for six Irish sisters.
subfiles.summary: The minister identifies Joan Twomey as Sister St. Joan of Arc and names Mother Saint Genevieve in Tokyo as the sisters' superior.

subfiles.title: Visa Division routing note on three religious sisters
subfiles.about: Transfer of applications for Ana Segurola, Rosa Carola Gorini, and another sister.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten note says Justice Department contact Miss Davis delivered the three cases and the applicants were ready to leave.

subfiles.title: Rosa Carola Gorini alien departure application
subfiles.about: Permission for an Italian religious sister to leave the United States for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Gorini applies for departure permission to undertake religious and educational work in Japan for the Society of the Sacred Heart. The form records her Italian birth and residence history, Philadelphia contacts, alien registration, personal description, and notarized witness affidavit.

subfiles.title: Ana Segurola alien departure application
subfiles.about: Permission for a Spanish religious sister to leave the United States for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Segurola applies to depart for Japan in connection with Sacred Heart religious work. The form records her birth in Azpeitia, Spanish residence history, passport and alien-registration details, Philadelphia contacts, physical description, and notarized affidavit.

subfiles.title: Mercedes Ruiz-Huerta Horne alien departure application
subfiles.about: Permission for a Spanish religious sister to leave the United States for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Ruiz-Huerta Horne applies to travel to Japan for Sacred Heart educational work. Her application supplies Spanish residence and passport information, Philadelphia references, alien registration, personal description, funding by her congregation, and a notarized witness affidavit.

subfiles.title: Colombian acknowledgment of Circular No. 8
subfiles.about: Receipt and transmission of SCAP entry-and-exit regulations.
subfiles.summary: The Colombian chargé acknowledges the January 17 communication and reports forwarding Circular No. 8 to Colombia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

subfiles.title: Request to bypass normal records clearance for military permits
subfiles.about: Proposed exception allowing direct contact with Commander Millett.
subfiles.summary: Hibbard asks whether SPD may communicate directly with Millett on Japan travel permits, as the Visa and Passport divisions already do.

subfiles.title: Procedure for transmitting Japan entry requests to the Joint Chiefs
subfiles.from: M. E. Wolberg, Special Projects Division
subfiles.about: Establishing a direct process for military-permit applications under Circular No. 8.
subfiles.summary: Wolberg reviews how the Visa and Passport divisions communicate with the Military Permit Secretariat and proposes that SPD likewise send requests directly to Commander Millett. She discusses required information, possible forms, records clearance, and messenger service.

subfiles.title: Iraqi acknowledgment of Circular No. 8
subfiles.about: Receipt and transmission of procedures for civilian entry into Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Iraqi Minister acknowledges Circular No. 8 and reports sending its application procedures to the appropriate Iraqi authorities.

subfiles.title: Chilean acknowledgment of Circular No. 8
subfiles.about: Receipt of SCAP regulations governing people, aircraft, and vessels.
subfiles.summary: Chile's ambassador acknowledges receipt of the January 17 note and two copies of Circular No. 8.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Military Permit Secretariat about three sisters
subfiles.from: M. E. Wolberg, Special Projects Division
subfiles.about: Routing any SCAP decisions concerning three religious sisters to SPD.
subfiles.summary: Flickinger agrees that any clearance information received for Ruiz-Huerta Horne, Segurola, or Gorini will be sent to Wolberg's division.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning Argentine repatriates and a naval vessel
subfiles.to: Martin Luis Drago, Argentine chargé d'affaires ad interim
subfiles.about: Unsuccessful attempt to place prospective repatriates aboard an Argentine naval vessel.
subfiles.summary: The Department reports that the vessel arrived at Kobe and departed before the Yokohama office could assemble the prospective passengers. Telegrams produced only one reply, from Jorge Yamamoto, who did not then wish to return; locating and preparing others would require several weeks.

subfiles.title: Internal checks on Mercedes Ruiz-Huerta Horne
subfiles.from: M. E. Wolberg, Special Projects Division
subfiles.about: Results of agency checks on Ruiz-Huerta Horne.
subfiles.summary: FC, ES, and VD reported no information concerning Mercedes Ruiz-Huerta Horne; her departure application was attached.

subfiles.title: Internal checks on Rosa Carola Gorini
subfiles.from: M. E. Wolberg, Special Projects Division
subfiles.about: Results of agency checks on Gorini.
subfiles.summary: FC, ES, and VD reported no information concerning Rosa Carola Gorini; her departure application was attached.

subfiles.title: Conversations with Mrs. McGranery about the sisters' applications
subfiles.from: M. E. Wolberg, Special Projects Division
subfiles.about: Expediting entry applications for three religious sisters traveling to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Wolberg explains new exit and SCAP entry procedures to Mrs. McGranery, who says the sisters will teach children of U.S. military personnel. Wolberg supplies the eleven required application details and directs the Spanish applications to Germán Baraibar and the Italian application to Mr. Martinez, unless their superior has already applied in Japan.

subfiles.title: Memorandum confirming Rosa Carola Gorini's clearance
subfiles.about: Military permission granted for Gorini to travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Department informs the Italian Embassy that occupation authorities have approved Mother Gorini's entry into Japan.

subfiles.title: Instructions to Mrs. McGranery for the sisters' Japan applications
subfiles.from: Robert B. Clattenburg Jr., Special Projects Division
subfiles.about: Required diplomatic and personal information for three religious sisters seeking entry to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Clattenburg confirms that no new action is needed if the sisters' superior has already applied in Japan. Otherwise the Spanish and Italian embassies must submit their cases under Circular No. 8, supported by eleven specified biographical, travel, passport, work, and maintenance details; approved travelers need no U.S. exit permit.

subfiles.title: Call to Spanish Embassy about Segurola and Ruiz-Huerta Horne
subfiles.from: M. E. Wolberg, Special Projects Division
subfiles.about: Identification of the Spanish official handling Japan travel applications.
subfiles.summary: Mrs. Parks advises that the sisters' cases should be addressed to Chargé d'Affaires Germán Baraibar.

subfiles.title: Call to Italian Embassy about Rosa Carola Gorini
subfiles.from: M. E. Wolberg, Special Projects Division
subfiles.about: Identification of the Italian Embassy contact for Gorini's application.
subfiles.summary: Mr. Martinez says applications by Italian nationals should be sent to the embassy for his attention.

subfiles.title: Danish request for additional copies of Circular No. 8
subfiles.about: Copies of Japanese travel regulations for Danish consular representatives.
subfiles.summary: The Danish Minister requests six copies of Circular No. 8 for distribution to Danish consular representatives in the United States.

subfiles.title: Department reply transmitting Circular No. 8 to Denmark
subfiles.about: Provision of six additional copies of SCAP Circular No. 8.
subfiles.summary: The Department acknowledges Denmark's request and encloses six additional copies of the circular.

subfiles.title: Spanish request for Gonzalo de Ojeda's entry documents
subfiles.about: Travel documents for Spain's newly appointed minister to Japan and his family.
subfiles.summary: Spain reports that occupation authorities have cleared Gonzalo de Ojeda and his family and asks the Department to forward documents permitting entry.

subfiles.title: Conversation on documentation for Gonzalo de Ojeda's family
subfiles.from: M. E. Wolberg, Special Projects Division
subfiles.about: Documents required for the Ojeda family's travel and entry into Japan.
subfiles.summary: Wolberg advises Sanz-Briz that passports plus English statements confirming SCAP clearance are sufficient for departure; Japan will issue entry permits at the port of entry.

subfiles.title: Memorandum to Spain confirming documentation for the Ojeda family
subfiles.about: Written confirmation of travel-document requirements under Circular No. 8.
subfiles.summary: The Department explains that each member of the Ojeda family must carry a passport or equivalent document and an English statement from an authorized Spanish representative confirming SCAP clearance and supplying the information required by paragraph 7(b). No additional U.S. departure documents are needed; Japanese entry permits will be issued at the port of entry.
